question: Describe the love of the Holy Prophet (سم الله عليه وآله واصحابه وسلم) for his household in the light of Ahadith.
answer: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) had deep and immense love for his household (Ahl-e-Bait), and many Ahadith describe this love. He declared: "I have left among you two things. As long as you are attached to them, you can never get astray. It is the Book of Allah and my household (Ahl-e-Bait)." (Sunan Tirmizi: 3786). Hazrat Ayesha reports that the Holy Prophet once called Hazrat Fatima Al-Zahra, Hazrat Ali, Hazrat Hassan and Hazrat Hussain, covered them with a mantle and prayed: "O Allah! These are my household, remove impurity from them and make them pure." (Hadith al-Kisa). Whenever he passed by the house of Hazrat Fatima on his way to prayer, he used to call: "Namaz, O household, may Allah remove impurity from you." (Sunan Tirmizi: 3206). About his grandsons he said: "These two (Hassan and Hussain) are my sons. I love them, O Allah! Love them and also those who love them." (Sunan Tirmizi: 3775). About Hazrat Fatima he said: "Fatima is a part of me, and he who makes her angry, makes me angry." Hazrat Abu Hurairah reports that the Holy Prophet said: "The best among you is he who takes care of my household after me." Thus his love for his household was a model of affection and honour which all Muslims are commanded to follow.
explanation: Drawn from the lesson text which cites Sunan Tirmizi (3786, 3206, 3775), Sahih al-Bukhari and Hadith al-Kisa describing the Prophet's love for Ahl-e-Bait.

question: What do you know about the Mothers of Faithful?
answer: The wives of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) are titled "Ummahat ul Muminen" (the mothers of all believers), as Allah Almighty says: "And the wives of the Prophet are the mothers of the believers." (Surah Al-Ahzab: 6). Their number is eleven; two of them died during the lifetime of the Holy Prophet and nine lived with him until the last days of his life. The most prominent among them are: (1) Umm Al-Mu'minin Hazrat Khadija bint Khuwailad (RA) — the first woman to believe in the Holy Prophet, whom he married when she was 40; all his offspring, except Hazrat Ibrahim, were from her; she dedicated all her wealth to Islam and passed away at the age of 60 in the 10th year of Prophethood. (2) Umm Al-Mu'minin Hazrat Ayesha Siddiqa (RA) bint Abu Bakr Siddique — married in Shawwal 11th year of Prophethood, one of the most prominent jurist women of the Ummah, very brave and courageous; she healed the wounds of the Prophet in the Battle of Uhud and passed away on 17th Ramadan, 57 A.H., buried in Jannat-ul-Baqi. (3) Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaima (RA), called "Umm Al-Masakin" (Mother of the poor) because she fed the poor very much. (4) Hazrat Zainab bint Jahash (RA), a very pious and generous woman who died at 53 in 20 A.H. The other purified wives are Hazrat Sawda bint Zama'ah, Hazrat Hafsa bint Umar bin Khattab, Hazrat Umm-e-Salma bint Abu Umayyah, Hazrat Juwairiya bint Al-Harith, Hazrat Umm-e-Habiba Ram'la bint Abu Sufyan, Hazrat Safia bint Huyai bin Akh'tab, Hazrat Maimuna bint Harith, and Hazrat Maria Qibtia (RA) (sent as a gift by Muqawqas, the King of Egypt, and mother of Hazrat Ibrahim). Allah also addressed them: "O wives of the Prophet! You are not like the ordinary women of the world..." (Surah Al-Ahzab: 32). All his purified wives are the family members and the beacons of guidance for the Muslim Ummah.
explanation: Based on the lesson section "The Purified wives", listing the Ummahat ul Muminen and the Qur'anic verse of Surah Al-Ahzab (6 and 32).

question: What is meant by 'Manaqib'?
answer: The word "Manaqib" is an Arabic word; its singular is "Manqabat", which means praise, good deeds, qualities and virtues. In technical terms, the achievements and virtues of a famous personality are called "Manqabat", whether in prose or poetry — such as the praise, qualities and virtues of Ahl-e-Bait Athar, religious leaders and the companions.
explanation: Definition taken directly from the opening section "The meaning and concept of the word Manaqib".

question: Who are Ahl e Bait?
answer: The word "Ahl" in Arabic means eligible or member, and "Bayt" means "home", so Ahl al-Bayt means family. According to the Qur'anic term, "Ahl-e-Bayt" refers to the family of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), which includes his wives and children. The Holy Qur'an has declared his wives as "Ummahat ul Muminen" (the mothers of all believers). In the light of Hadith al-Kisa and Surah Al-Ahzab (33), the Ahl-e-Bait include the Holy Prophet, his purified wives, his offspring, Hazrat Ali, Hazrat Fatima Al-Zahra, Hazrat Hassan and Hazrat Hussain.
explanation: Compiled from the lesson's definition of Ahl-e-Bayt and the Hadith al-Kisa passage on images 121-122.

question: Write down the rights of Ahl e Bait.
answer: The rights of the household of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) are: (1) We must love them. (2) We must obey them. (3) We must believe in their justness. (4) We must love those who love them and detest those who keep hatred for them. We should also develop immense love for the Ahl-e-Bait, abide by their teachings and follow their footsteps so that we may gain the nearness of the Holy Prophet and his intercession on the Day of Judgement.
explanation: Listed explicitly in the lesson under the heading "Rights of Ahl e Bait".

question: Outline the names of Ahl e Bait in the light of Hadith al-Kisa.
answer: According to Hadith al-Kisa, Hazrat Ayesha reports that the Holy Prophet (PBUH) called upon Hazrat Fatima Al-Zahra, Hazrat Ali, Hazrat Hassan and Hazrat Hussain, and covered them with a mantle and prayed: "O Allah! These are my household, remove impurity from them and make them pure." Thus the Ahl-e-Bait named in Hadith al-Kisa are Hazrat Fatima Al-Zahra, Hazrat Ali, Hazrat Hassan and Hazrat Hussain, together with the Holy Prophet himself.
explanation: Taken from the passage describing Hadith al-Kisa in the lesson.

question: Write down a note on the excellence of companions.
answer: By virtue of the blessed company of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), the companions (Sahaba) achieved a high status and excellence that anyone afterwards can never attain. As the chain of Prophethood is over and no one can be a companion without the company of a Prophet, their rank is unique. They spent their lives in the period which the Holy Prophet declared to be "The Best", saying: "The best people among you are the ones who belong to my lifetime period, then those who would come afterwards, then those who would come afterwards." Allah Almighty declared His pleasure with all of them, saying: "And leading everyone, the first are the Muhajirs and the Ansar, and those who followed them with virtue — Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him... this is the greatest success." (Surah At-Tauba: 100). They are the highest-ranking people in the world after the Prophets. They passed on to us the Holy Qur'an, the Sunnah and the entire Deen, and Islam reached every corner of the world due to the efforts of their sacrifice. Hence to have devout love and reverence for all the companions is the requisite of faith, and the slightest disrespect or blasphemy of any companion is a great sin; the Holy Prophet said: "Do not insult my Companions, for if anyone of you spends gold equal to Mount Uhud (in Allah's cause), it will not be equal to a Mudd, or even half a Mudd, spent by one of them." (Bukhari: 3673 / Muslim: 222). Therefore it is obligatory upon all Muslims to love and revere all the companions of the Holy Prophet.
explanation: Based on the section "Excellence of Companions" in the lesson, citing Surah At-Tauba (100) and Bukhari/Muslim hadith on not insulting the companions.

question: Explain the greatness of companions.
answer: The greatness of the companions (Sahaba) is established both by the Qur'an and by the Ahadith of the Holy Prophet (PBUH). The Holy Prophet said: "Glad tidings for the one who saw me and for the one as well who saw the person who has seen me" — thereby giving glad tidings to the companions (Sahaba) and their successors (Tabi'in). He also said: "The best people among you are the ones who belong to my lifetime period, then those who would come afterwards, then those who would come afterwards." Almighty Allah declared His pleasure with all of them in the Holy Qur'an: "And leading everyone, the first are the Muhajirs and the Ansar, and those who followed them with virtue — Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him, and He has kept ready for them Gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide in it forever and ever; this is the greatest success." (Surah At-Tauba: 100). These auspicious personalities who attained the status of Sahaba are the highest-ranking people in the world after the Prophets. They spent their lives in the era declared "The Best" by the Prophet and they transmitted to us the Holy Qur'an, the Sunnah and the entire Deen, so that Islam reached every corner of the world through their sacrifice. Therefore, it is obligatory upon all Muslims to love and revere all the companions, and disrespecting any of them is a great sin.
explanation: Drawn from the section "Greatness of Companions (Sahaba)" and "Excellence of Companions", quoting the Prophet's hadith and Surah At-Tauba (100).

question: Describe the literal and terminological meaning of Sahabi (Companion).
answer: The word "Sahabi" is derived from an Arabic word "Suhb", which is meant for "companionship". In Islamic terminology, a Sahabi (or companion) is someone who met with the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in the state of faith and passed away with faith.
explanation: Definition given directly in the opening section of the lesson on the greatness of companions.

question: What is the literal meaning of 'Ashra Mubasharah'?
answer: In Arabic, "Ashra" stands for ten, and "Mubasharah" is derived from the word "Bisharah", which means "the one who is given good news". Thus, "Ashra Mubasharah" literally means the ten companions whom the Holy Prophet (PBUH) gave the glad tidings of Paradise.
explanation: Explained in the lesson section "The Ten Blessed Companions".

question: Outline the names of the Ten Blessed Companions.

question: Write down an essay on the importance, significance and benefits of knowledge.
answer: Knowledge is the greatest blessing of Almighty Allah among His exclusive favours on human beings. The first quality conferred to Prophet Adam (AS) right after his creation was knowledge, and Allah states: "And Allah the Supreme taught Adam all the names (of things)." (Surah Al-Baqarah: 31). Almighty Allah declared human beings the best creation and blessed them with wisdom and knowledge; the entire universe has been made under the control of humans through knowledge, and man has superiority over other creations due to knowledge. Knowledge is the basis of all excellence and the means of transcendence. It is itself an attribute of Allah, the Knower of all hidden things and the Knower of inside hearts. The world was unaware of the importance of knowledge when Islam began in Arabia; Islam highlighted the value of knowledge and encouraged people to acquire it. About the significance of knowledge and scholars the Holy Qur'an says: "Allah will raise the believers among you, and those given knowledge, to high ranks." (Surah Al-Mujadilah: 58,11) and "My Lord, bestow me more knowledge." (Surah Taha: 114) and "Are the knowledgeable and the ignorant equal?" (Surah Az-Zumar: 39,9). The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: "Scholars are the heirs of Prophets." (Sunan Tirmizi: 2682); "A single knowledgeable believer is harder on Satan than a thousand devout worshippers." (Sunan Ibn-e-Majah: 222); and "To acquire knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim (male and female)." Good morals and manners — including the distinction between right and wrong, sense of good and evil, recognition of the Creator and Master, and love and kindness with the creation — are developed in a person if he is groomed under the shade of knowledge and morality. As a result, the person gets dignified in character and habits and becomes a valuable citizen. Therefore, seeking knowledge is considered an obligation in Islam, and moral grooming of our subordinates, offspring and family is also our responsibility; knowledge and morality are indispensable to each other. In fact, the basis of all morals and other qualities is knowledge, which has to be preferred by every Muslim.
explanation: Compiled from the lesson "Importance and Excellence of Knowledge", including the Qur'anic verses (Al-Baqarah 31, Al-Mujadilah 58:11, Taha 114, Az-Zumar 39:9) and Ahadith of Tirmizi and Ibn-e-Majah.

question: Describe the meaning and concept of knowledge.
answer: The literal meaning of "knowledge" is to know and become aware of; however, the word "education" is used to pass on knowledge to others and to teach. Terminologically, knowledge stands for knowing the reality of something through the five senses and the intellect. Knowledge is the greatest blessing of Almighty Allah, and the first quality conferred to Prophet Adam right after his creation was knowledge.
explanation: Based on the section "The Concept and Meaning of Knowledge" in the lesson.

question: Write down a note on the significance of family in Islam.
answer: The word "Khandan" (family) is a Persian word meaning a household, family, tribe, offspring and ancestry; domestic life stands for the gathering of close relatives of a clan. By nature a man cannot live all alone; he likes to live combined with the population of a house, area, village or city. Parents, husband and wife, and offspring have a crucial position in a family, and the family group extends to grandparents, paternal and maternal uncles and aunts and their offspring. Domestic life is the first step of one's cultural and social life, and since all humans love to live with their family and relatives due to their social instinct, the family is the basic unit of society. Social life begins with a clan and family, and a clan is established with the marriage of a male and a female. Because of this, Islam gives equal importance to men and women; each is restricted within defined boundaries and Islam emphasizes the fulfilment of everyone's rights and obligations. Allah Almighty says: "O mankind! We have indeed created you from one man and one woman." (Surah Al-Hujurat: 49,13). The concept of relations, family and clan is found only among humans in creation, and this status is conferred on man, the best of creation, so that he expresses love, respect and kindness to parents, grandparents, siblings and offspring. A man earns and fulfils the needs of the family, and if someone gets annoyed he tries to resolve the issue. All these factors are exhibited due to the existence of a family; therefore, Islam considers the family a beauty for society and a pious community.
explanation: Compiled from the opening sections "The Concept and Meaning of a Family" and "The Beginning of Family and its Social Significance", quoting Surah Al-Hujurat (49:13).

question: Explain the rights and obligations of husband and wife.
answer: The existence and sustenance of humanity is based on the relationship between a man and a woman, so the relationship of husband and wife has an important place among all human relationships. A marriage bond is established after the parents' consent from both sides and the process of requesting and accepting the Nikkah; the Holy Qur'an named this bond "Ahsaun", meaning to be protected within a fortress. Nikkah is an agreement through which husband and wife become lifelong companions and benefactors of one another; they share sorrows and happiness and help each other in difficult times. The Holy Prophet said: "Marriage is part of my Sunnah, and whoever does not follow my Sunnah has nothing to do with me." (Sunan Ibn-e-Majah: 1846). Allah also says: "They (women) are coverings for you, and you are coverings for them." (Surah Al-Baqarah: 2, 187). The Holy Prophet said: "Each of you is a guardian, and each of you will be asked about his subjects." (Sahih Bukhari: 2409). According to Islam there are rights enjoined on both husband and wife for each other; Allah says: "And the women also have rights similar to those of men over them." (Surah Al-Baqarah: 228). The rights of the wife over the husband include the provision of sustenance, dress, home (shelter), medication and other needs as per his financial position. The woman can use the amount of dower in any business within Shariah limitations or keep it to herself. The man is also obliged to behave nicely with his wife and other family members, not to oppress or do injustice in any way, to keep an attitude of benevolence and to fulfil all rights according to Shariah guidance. The wife is responsible for protecting her husband's wealth and provisions like a trust in his absence and should not allow any stranger to enter the home without her husband's permission; Allah says: "So virtuous women are the reverent ones, guarding behind their husbands the way Allah has decreed guarding." (Surah Al-Nisa: 34). She should not demand any expense beyond the financial position of her husband, should not needlessly discuss her difficulties or scarcity of wealth with others (rather she should endure and forgive), should not reveal the secrets of the home, should secure and nurture the children with proper guidance, and should serve her husband and obey him. The Holy Prophet said: "The best of you is he who is best to his family, and I am the best among you to my family." (Sunan Ibn-e-Majah: 2053).
explanation: Compiled from the section "The Relationship of Husband and Wife" and "Obligations and Rights of Husband and Wife", citing Surah Al-Baqarah (2:187, 228), Surah Al-Nisa (34), Sahih Bukhari (2409) and Sunan Ibn-e-Majah (1846, 2053).

question: What is meant by a family?
answer: "Khandan" (family) is a Persian word which means a household, family, tribe, offspring and ancestry; domestic life stands for the gathering of close relatives of a clan. A family includes parents, husband and wife, offspring, grandparents, and paternal and maternal uncles and aunts with their offspring. It is the basic unit of society and the first step of one's cultural and social life.
explanation: Based on "The Concept and Meaning of a Family" section of the lesson.

question: Write about the respect of parents.
answer: The relationship with parents is the most important and respectful of all relations, as they are the means of our life in the world and all our strength is built up due to their care and upbringing; therefore we should not show any negligence in respect and service to our parents. Allah orders us: "And your Lord has ordained that you do not worship anyone except Him, and treat your parents with kindness; if either of them or both reach old age in your presence, do not say 'Uff' to them and do not rebuff them, and speak to them with the utmost respect. And lower your wing humbly for them, with mercy, and pray, 'My Lord! Have mercy on them both, the way they nursed me when I was young.'" (Surah Al-Asra: 23, 24). It is the obligation of the offspring to respect their parents, obey them, serve them and treat them nicely even if they are infidels or polytheists; however, the offspring should excuse if they order something of disbelief or polytheism. It is also instructed to have a good relationship with the relatives and friends of parents, to thank them and to pray for their forgiveness.
explanation: Based on the section "Respect of Parents", quoting Surah Al-Asra (17:23-24).

question: Describe the rights of offspring.
answer: Offspring are the buoyancy of a family; their objective is the sustenance of humanity and they are the great blessing of Almighty Allah. The rights of offspring (which are the obligations of parents) include: good upbringing, arranging quality education and guidance, kindness and affection, marrying them into a good family, maintaining justice in inheritance, giving them necessary religious knowledge, teaching them the knowledge of the Holy Qur'an, the performance of prayers and Islamic values, maintaining equality and justice in treatment, including daughters in love and gifts, not being ungrateful at the birth of a daughter, and avoiding torturing or over-strictness while keeping behaviour of love and tenderness and not killing any offspring due to fear of hunger or poverty.
explanation: Compiled from the section "Rights of Offspring" in the lesson.

question: Write own ten points on the dignity of humanity.
answer: (1) "Dignity" stands for respect, excellence and greatness; the dignity of humanity means each human has respect and greatness in this universe. (2) Humans are titled "Ashraf ul Makhluqaat" — the best creation of Almighty Allah on the earth — and therefore have superiority over all other creations. (3) Allah has created all things on earth, heaven and between them for the benefit and ease of humans, and all things are the collective heritage of humans. (4) The Holy Qur'an declares this honour: "Indeed We have honoured the Descendants of Adam and transported them over land and sea, and gave them good things as sustenance, and made them better than most of Our creation." (Surah Al-Asra: 70). (5) A human receives the blessing of speech, knowledge and wisdom through which he becomes eligible to explain his feelings adequately. (6) Islam negates the differences of caste, colour, language and country. (7) The criteria of greatness and excellence is piety and fear of Allah: "Indeed the more honourable among you, in the sight of Allah, is one who is more pious among you." (Surah Al-Hujurat: 13). (8) All humans in this world are from one origin — from a single soul — as stated in Surah Al-Nisa: 1. (9) Allah has made man His deputy and vicegerent on earth and freed him from the slavery of false gods; no one has superiority over another except in faith, knowledge and piety. (10) Every human should protect the life, respect and property of other humans who belong to the nation and country without distinction of caste, colour, religion and language, and should avoid all acts that are against the dignity of humanity, such as pride, degrading others, oppression and injustice, spying, unequal treatment of offspring, taunting people or using foul language.
explanation: Compiled from the sections "Concept of the Dignity of Humanity" and "Significance of the Dignity of Humanity" and the list of "Actions that are against Dignity of Humanity", citing Surah Al-Asra 70, Al-Hujurat 13 and Al-Nisa 1.

question: What does Holy Quran order us about the dignity of humanity?
answer: The Holy Qur'an establishes the dignity of humanity in very clear terms. Allah says: "Indeed We have honoured the Descendants of Adam and transported them over land and sea, and gave them good things as sustenance, and made them better than most of Our creation." (Surah Al-Asra: 70). This shows that Allah has bestowed very high excellence on humans over all creations and has made all things on earth, heaven and between them for their benefit and ease. The Qur'an also declares that the criterion of greatness is not caste, colour, language or country but piety: "Indeed the more honourable among you, in the sight of Allah, is one who is more pious among you." (Surah Al-Hujurat: 13). It further teaches that all humans are from one origin: "Created you from a single soul and from it created its spouse and from them, both has spread the multitude of men and women." (Surah Al-Nisa: 1). Allah has made man His deputy and vicegerent on earth, released him from the slavery of false gods and made him responsible and dignified, bound to abide only by Allah's commandments. No one has superiority over any other person except in faith, knowledge and piety, and these verses address every human, whether Muslim or non-Muslim.
explanation: The answer quotes and explains the Qur'anic verses (Surah Al-Asra 70, Al-Hujurat 13, Al-Nisa 1) used in the lesson on the dignity of humanity.

question: Describe the concept of dignity of humanity.
answer: "Dignity" stands for respect, excellence and greatness; thus the dignity of humanity stands for the respect and greatness of humans. Humans are titled "Ashraf ul Makhluqaat", the best creation of Almighty Allah on earth, and therefore have superiority over all other creations. The dignity of humanity means each human should protect the life, respect and property of other humans who belong to the nation and country without distinction of caste, colour, religion and language.
explanation: Taken directly from the section "Concept of the Dignity of Humanity" in the lesson.

question: Write down the conditions which are against the dignity of humanity.
answer: Man has a distinctive status due to piety and good manners, but there are many habits which are against the dignity of humanity, such as: pride (considering oneself superior in knowledge, wealth, caste or wisdom before Allah or creation); degrading people, making fun of them, accusing them or adopting a disrespectful attitude; oppressing and doing injustice to people and finding defects and spying on them; behaving unequally with offspring by distinguishing between younger and older, wise and unwise, and sons and daughters; taunting any human being because of physical shortcoming or error, calling people bad names and disrespecting them; and talking in a bad manner with foul words and unfriendly ways.
explanation: Compiled from the list under "Actions that are against Dignity of Humanity" in the lesson.
